title: Equivalent Ratios
objective: I can find and check equivalent ratios using multiplication and division.
model: ratio table / batches of a recipe scaled by one factor applied to both terms

widgets.component: review warm-up (rate times time, gallons per minute, muffin flour, cheaper store)
widgets.root: Matches the lesson's own warm-up; keys correct (120 pages, 12 min, 5 cups, Store B $1.20 versus $1.25).

widgets.component: equivalent-ratio recognition, not-equivalent, simplest form, $45 for 3 hours
widgets.root: Keys correct (4:10, 2:3, 3:5, 3:5, $120). Distractors are the additive and swapped-order errors.

widgets.component: added the multiplier (5 + 3); divided the two parts by different numbers (12 ÷ 6, 18 ÷ 3)
widgets.root: The two real misconceptions of the lesson; e indexes verified.

widgets.component: three ratio rows, one missing term each (3:7 = 9:?, 5:8 = ?:24, 4:6 = ?:3)
widgets.root: Includes a scale-down row; answers 21, 15, 2 correct.
Generated, correct (L3 puts the unknown first). Bare fill-ins, but the manipulable model is offered right beside them in 4.7.

widgets.component: mixing station: build batches until one term matches, then type the other term
widgets.root: A manipulable ratio table of batches; the miss text separates 'added instead of multiplied' from 'wrong term'.

widgets.component: 'scale factor from 3 cups of yogurt to 15 cups', 'How many cups of strawberries are needed?', 'Why must both ingredients be multiplied by the same factor?'
widgets.root: The smoothie recipe (2 cups of strawberries for every 3 of yogurt, 2:3) is never stated in the three stems or a viz. 5.2 cannot be answered at all; 5.3 asks about 'both ingredients' and '2:3' with no recipe in view.
widgets.replacement: Make the three items one stand-alone scenario with a ratio-table viz: 'A smoothie uses 2 cups of strawberries for every 3 cups of yogurt. Mia uses 15 cups of yogurt.' 5.1 key 5 (scale factor), 5.2 key 10 strawberries, 5.3 keep the conceptual key ('so the ratio stays 2:3'). Keep the existing distractors (3, 12, 45 and 5, 12, 15) because they are the additive and product errors.

widgets.root: Key $24 correct, $40 is the additive-in-reverse error.

widgets.component: missing numbers, up to a two-blank chain (7:2 = ?:4 = 35:?)
add-versus-multiply error, prove two ways, simplify-to-compare table, 4:6 = ?:15, 12:20 table, soprano/alto 40 singers, 6:9 mix
widgets.root: Keys recomputed (10 rock songs, 24 sopranos, 3 / 15 / 50 / 21 in the drum table, 10:15). Cross-multiplying appears in 2.2 only as one of three allowed methods and is taught by this lesson itself.

widgets.where: Challenge §3 (act:ratiomix recipe L3, equivalent L4; sort)
widgets.component: build batches to a goal, test a claimed ratio, simplify and sort into 2:3 / 3:4 / 5:6 presets
widgets.root: Manipulable batches; sort cards all simplify as stated (8:12, 12:18, 20:30 -> 2:3 and so on).

widgets.component: subtracting to compare, different divisors, 'same two numbers' (3:2 versus 2:3), cross products 6/8 and 9/12, 28:42 simplest, 35 pages for 20 musicians, 150 min for 20 min, 24 spotlights
widgets.root: Keys correct (28 headphone sets, 3:4, 21 pages, 60 min, 66 lights, 6 × 12 = 8 × 9 = 72). Cross products are taught in this lesson (its config's method 2), so 5.3 is in scope.
